channels.label: SIGNAL
paragraphs: I build the worlds the camera believes in. Flats, facades, breakaways, rigs — scenic construction for film and television, from first draft to final strike.
Comfortable in timber, steel, foam, and whatever the art director dreamed up at 2am.

projects.title: Period Storefront Facade
projects.desc: Full-scale 1940s high street exterior. Three storefronts, practical doors and glazing, aged brick finish over timber frame. Built in sections for a night shoot turnaround.
projects.caption: CAM 1
projects.writeup:
Commissioned for a wartime drama shooting nights on a back-lot street. The brief: three adjoining 1940s storefronts with practical doors, openable sash windows, and glazing safe enough to play action against.

Built as six craned-in sections over a steel spine so the facade could land on uneven tarmac and still read dead level on camera. Brick finish is carved and scumbled foam over ply skins — close enough that the DP asked which street we'd found.

projects.title: Breakaway Wall Rig
projects.desc: Stunt-rated breakaway wall with resettable panels, engineered for six takes. Balsa core, scored plaster skin, hidden steel safety frame.
projects.caption: CAM 2
projects.writeup:
A stunt performer goes through this wall six times in one day, and the wall has to look identical in every take. Balsa framing with a scored plaster skin, backed by a hidden steel goalpost frame that keeps the surrounding set rigid.

Reset time got down to eleven minutes by take three — pre-cut replacement panels, keyed fixings, and a two-person drill we rehearsed like a pit stop.

projects.title: Late Night: The Miniature Hour
projects.desc: 1:8 scale city block for a destruction sequence. Cast plaster buildings with frangible cores, wired for pyro cues.
projects.caption: CAM 3
projects.writeup:
A city block at 1:8 scale, built to be destroyed exactly once. Cast plaster buildings with frangible cores, pre-weakened along planned failure lines and wired for pyro cues.

Everything was documented brick-by-brick beforehand so the VFX team could rebuild it digitally for the previz — then we blew up the real one.

projects.title: Competition Workshop Set
projects.desc: Modular workshop bays for a fabrication competition series. Identical stations, overnight resets between episodes, camera hides built into the racking.
projects.caption: CAM 1

projects.title: Brand Activation Facade
projects.desc: Walk-through storefront installation for a product launch — three rooms, practical lighting, built to survive six weeks of foot traffic instead of six days of shooting.
projects.caption: CAM 1

blocks.text: I'm Ben — carpenter, designer, and general solver of impossible requests for film and television construction. When a script calls for a place that doesn't exist, my job is to make it exist by call time.
With over a decade of experience as a carpenter, in the real world and on set .Most days you'll find me somewhere between the drafting table and the shop floor.
Off the clock it's balcony geraniums, a cat who supervises all my sketching, and a glass of something cold while the sun goes down. The tools get put away — the habit of building things doesn't.
